caption: A drop of red food colouring is added to a glass of white icing and stirred, and the icing turns pink.

sa.check: A container of white icing is present.
Red food colouring is added to it.
The colouring is a single drop.
The order is drop, stir, pink.

pc.expect: Colour spreads from the drop through the icing as it is stirred; coloured areas stay coloured, and the pink deepens or evens out but never returns to white.
pc.fail: The icing turns white again where it was pink; or the red gathers back into a drop; or the pink appears before the drop lands; or the colour flickers.

pc.expect: The result is pink, a lighter tint of the red, with red streaks where unmixed; the white stays white until the colour reaches it.
pc.fail: The icing turns a colour other than pink or red; or the red streaks turn white instead of blending; or the icing becomes darker red than the drop itself.

pc.expect: The icing behaves as a thick paste: the spoon leaves furrows, streaks stay where drawn until stirred, and the drop sits on it rather than dispersing like ink in water.
pc.fail: The icing flows like water and the colour disperses in swirls on its own; or the icing is rigid and the spoon passes through it without marking; or it bounces like rubber.

pc.expect: The icing moves only where stirred; the colouring does not spread faster than stirring carries it.
pc.fail: Colour spreads through unstirred icing on its own; or the icing swirls with no spoon; or the bowl turns by itself.

pc.expect: One container and one spoon; the amount of icing stays the same and nothing passes through the container.
pc.fail: The container fills or empties on its own; or a second spoon appears; or the spoon passes through the container; or the container changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The container, the spoon and the table keep their appearance.
pc.fail: The container changes colour; or the spoon changes; or the table pattern shifts.
